title: Fasten a spring-loaded access plate while maintaining its preload
instruction: Press the grey access plate level against its marked height while turning the three orange nuts down their studs. Keep the plate controlled as the nuts capture its spring load. Seat every nut against the plate, then withdraw both hands; the plate must remain level and compressed.
context: Three non-collinear fasteners capture the vertical preload and two-axis attitude of a spring-loaded access plate. One arm controls the plate while the other establishes real helical engagement and repeatedly regrips each nut.
setup: Bimanual YAM station, fixed layout and seed 0. Positions are metres, x forward, y left, z up. Tabletop z=0.7475. bracket is steel plate and threaded studs, mass 0.6 kg, collision envelope (0.25, 0.17, 0.047) m, initial position (0.265, 0, 0.7515000000000001), XYZW (0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 1.0). plate_carrier is a noncolliding simulation inertia link for the plate spring guide, mass 0.001 kg, collision envelope (0.001, 0.001, 0.001) m, initial position (0.265, 0, 0.7735000000000001), XYZW (0, 0, 0, 1). plate_gimbal is a noncolliding simulation inertia link for plate tilt, mass 0.001 kg, collision envelope (0.001, 0.001, 0.001) m, initial position (0.265, 0, 0.7735000000000001), XYZW (0, 0, 0, 1). pressure_plate is an aluminium rigid surrogate, mass 0.12 kg, collision envelope (0.25, 0.266, 0.032) m, initial position (0.265, 0, 0.7735000000000001), XYZW (0, 0, 0, 1). nut_0 is coarse threaded steel surrogate, mass 0.024 kg, collision envelope (0.034, 0.034, 0.01) m, initial position (0.15, -0.18, 0.7527), XYZW (0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 1.0). nut_1 is coarse threaded steel surrogate, mass 0.024 kg, collision envelope (0.034, 0.034, 0.01) m, initial position (0.36, -0.18, 0.7527), XYZW (0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 1.0). nut_2 is coarse threaded steel surrogate, mass 0.024 kg, collision envelope (0.034, 0.034, 0.01) m, initial position (0.22, 0.23, 0.7527), XYZW (0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 1.0). The two 1g carrier links are simulation coordinates, not separately manipulated objects; their 1mm boxes are noncolliding visualization proxies. Steel/aluminium names denote intended surrogates with prescribed masses and uncalibrated friction.
scoring: 0.2 for each of three correctly threaded nuts at its numeric seated pose, with at least3.4 measured turns and matching4mm pitch advance. 0.4 for retaining plate preload and attitude after all three nuts complete at least3.45 real turns. Full score requires the existing two-second released-hand stability hold. Dislodged goals lose credit. Invalid physics, lost parts or broken fixture preservation permanently score zero. Complete numeric predicates are in scene.json and SCORING.md.
run_limit: 18,000 control steps (900 simulated seconds at 20 Hz)
reset_notes: Native reset restores the authored layout and zero joint coordinates, settles through the official adapter, clears scorer history, and records a new episode. Native probes compare two reset repetitions within 3 mm. Seed 0; object_jitter=0.
fidelity: Coarse rigid helical thread facets model real contact-driven nut advance at4mm pitch. A400N/m prismatic spring and two passive tilt axes approximate plate compliance; two1g noncolliding links represent guide coordinates. Aluminium/steel parts use prescribed masses and uncalibrated friction. Enlarged grasp handles aid YAM access. Thread deformation, detailed thread friction and certified tightening torque are not modeled.
